title: Nine Collages: The New Graphics by Weingart
lede: Weingart’s poster and order form for his own series of nine hand-printed collages, laid out as a sheet of framed panels around one large collage.
summary: Black on white: a grid of framed collages with stepped lines, dot patterns, arcs, and crosses, and a vertical order form. Wolfgang Weingart, 1974–75.

source.label: Letterform Archive: Legacies of Swiss Style, Part 2—Wolfgang Weingart

evidence.note: Inspected Letterform Archive’s photograph of the Archive’s copy (2496 × 3000) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.

styles.note: Clear example. The small collages collect the style’s marks: spaced letters, stepped lines, dot fields, heavy bars, and halftone fragments.

context: Letterform Archive says the Nine Collages series came from darkroom experiments of the 1960s and early 1970s with “hand-cut films, barely-legible type, and the deliberate overlap of halftones to produce moiré effects”. [Letterform Archive](https://letterformarchive.org/news/from-the-collection-legacies-of-swiss-style-part-2-wolfgang-weingart/).
The poster text offers the collages, 59 × 49 cm, for sale by post from Basel, and its biography says Weingart taught typography at the School of Design in Basel from 1968.
observed: The title is set in heavy grotesque capitals across the top: “NINE COLLAGES: THE NEW GRAPHICS BY WEINGART”.
Thin rules divide the sheet into panels of different sizes. Each small panel shows one collage and a bold caption such as “COLLAGE 5/1974”.
Collage 6 is made of spaced letters and dots (“1 8 9-1”, “E”, “T”, “H”) scattered on white. Collage 5 has a stepped line, a small grid, arcs, and “STO?”.
The large central collage is a black flame-like shape that holds halftone photographs of a cemetery, a garden, and a woman, with black dots, short rays, and a white cross.
The sale text uses bold capitals with a much larger price. The order form at right is set vertically, with “Order Form” in large type.
The biography at the bottom left is set in a typewriter face.
interpretation: The poster shows that the style can use a plain framed grid as a container, as long as what happens inside the frames breaks it.
The typewriter biography is one of the few monospaced passages in Weingart’s work here; it is a small caption, not the main voice.
borrow: Frame small experiments in a grid of thin rules, with one bold caption under each.
Set a form or call to action vertically along one edge.
Scatter a few spaced letters and dots in open white space as a quiet panel next to dense ones.

rights.statement: No image is stored. Photograph by Letterform Archive. Weingart died in 2021, so the design is in copyright.
